detail: unit/48-claude-setup.test.ts: parsed .claude/settings.json and applied Claude Code's documented deny>ask>allow order. Every Makefile target (`make X`) resolves to allow. `werk accept|remove|restore` and `bun src/cli.ts accept|remove|restore` resolve to ask, also when a personal allow list holds Bash(werk:*), Bash(bun src/cli.ts:*) and Bash(*). Limit: Claude Code itself was not run; the precedence is simulated from its documented rules.

unit/48-claude-setup.test.ts: ran src/claude/lint-hook.ts with PostToolUse JSON on a temp copy (repo biome.json, git init, linked node_modules). A tsx file with an unused import and bad indent: exit 0, no output, file fixed on disk. A useEffect with a missing dependency: exit 2, stderr names useExhaustiveDependencies, file kept. After the dependency is added: exit 0, no output. settings.json wires the hook to Write|Edit|MultiEdit.

unit/48-claude-setup.test.ts: the check passes on the repo. In a temp root: links pass; a plain copy gives exit 1 with 'the file ... is a copy, not a link' naming the subagent; restoring the link passes; removing a link gives exit 1 'no link in the subagent folder' naming the subagent; a plain dev-only.md file is never named and does not fail the check.

unit/48-claude-setup.test.ts: allow list is exactly Bash(make:*), Bash(werk:*), Bash(bun src/cli.ts:*); no entry for curl/wget/ssh/rm/paths outside the repo. No mcpServers key, no .mcp.json, no .claude/skills, no tracked SKILL.md. `git check-ignore .claude/settings.local.json` exits 0. Caveat: `make install` and `make e2e` can fetch packages or the browser when missing; the entries themselves name no network or outside-write command.

unit/49-release-build.test.ts: ran `bun src/release/build.ts <tmp>/out`; exit 0. Found werk-darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, each with a .sha256 file whose digest equals the sha256 of the executable beside it. (Build writes dist/client in the checkout, a git-ignored build output.)

browser/49-executable.spec.ts: built the current-platform executable, copied only it into a new folder, ran it with a clean PATH/HOME. In a truly empty folder it refuses: 'has no git repository. git is required: run "git init" there.' (logged). After `git init` in that folder, it prints 'werk: serving on http://127.0.0.1:PORT'; the browser loads /p/<folder>, #screen and the Message composer show, no page error, no 4xx asset response. Only .git and .werk (the project's map folder) appear next to the executable; no extracted werk files. The git requirement is a design rule, judged not a failure.

browser/49-executable.spec.ts: `<exe> help` exits 0 and lists the same verb names, in the same order, as `bun src/cli.ts help` from the checkout (more than 10 verbs). `<exe> add root --title Root` and `<exe> show root` run from the folder, exit 0, show 'Root', no missing file/folder message.

browser/49-executable.spec.ts: started the executable, sent a chat message in the browser with the fake agent scripted for the chat role. The recorded launch's --append-system-prompt names every command as the quoted executable path (`"<dir>/werk" help`, `"<dir>/werk" add`), with no 'bun' word and no 'cli.ts'. A listed command (`<exe> search Root`) runs fine. Limit: the fake agent cannot run tools, so the agent actually running the command and answering from it was not observed; only the instruction it receives was.

unit/50-ci.test.ts: parsed .github/workflows/ci.yml. Triggers on push to main; ubuntu runner; checkout, then setup-bun, then separate steps `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test`, `make test-coverage`, `make e2e`, `make smoke` in that order, no continue-on-error. Each make target depends on the install stamp, which runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` on a clean checkout. `make smoke` runs build --current then smoke.ts (starts the executable, reads the map). Not observable: a real GitHub run, the green end state and the 'able to be released' badge.

unit/50-ci.test.ts: workflow also triggers on pull_request with no branch filter, runs the same single job with the same steps including `make smoke`, with no `|| true`. Not observable from the repo: the merge button state and the 'names the failed step' page; those depend on a GitHub required-status-check setting, which the repo cannot hold. Judged from workflow content only.

unit/50-ci.test.ts: in a copy of the app a type error file makes the typecheck command (`bun run typecheck`, what `make typecheck` runs) exit non-zero and name the file; the step is a separate `make typecheck` step, so the red step is named. The workflow has contents: read and no revert/reset/push, so the merge stays. Not observable: GitHub's red mark on the commit and any release gate; no werk code reads CI status for a follow-up ticket, the run log is the only basis.

unit/50-ci.test.ts: .bun-version holds an exact version (1.4.1). setup-bun uses `bun-version-file: .bun-version` with no literal version in ci.yml, and comes before the first make step. Every check target runs the bun-version guard (`make -n lint` shows the pinned value), so a new pin in the file is installed by the next run. Not observable: the real run log.

unit/50-ci.test.ts: ran `bun src/release/smoke.ts` against a fake executable that prints a serving line on a dead port, and against one that exits at once. Both exit non-zero, so `make smoke` and its CI step fail while the other steps stay green. Not observable: the red run state on GitHub.
